name: SHIPS
summary: A solar hidden-photon telescope at Hamburg Observatory and DESY.
detection_principle: Solar hidden photons oscillate into ordinary photons inside a Sun-pointing opaque high-vacuum tube; optics focus them onto a low-noise photomultiplier.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 2015 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Results from the Solar Hidden Photon Search (SHIPS)

collaboration.name: SHIPS Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No solar hidden-photon conversion signal; the 95% CL upper limit on the generated photon flux is approximately 25 mHz/m².

science_scope: Primarily searches for solar-produced axions or hidden photons as complementary tests of dark-matter candidates. Solar flux is distinct from cold Galactic-halo dark matter; a solar-axion discovery alone would not establish the composition of cosmic dark matter.
